Asobi 1.0 (build 1427) Oct 11, 2026

  • Repositions are read and noted. A scale, a move or an opacity change on a clip in a Premiere AAF is read and written out per clip, such as "Scaled 130%, moved 11.3% of the width right per the AAF". The Conform window tags those shots, its summary counts them, and each plate's header carries the line. It is never applied: a plate is the whole camera frame.
  • Moves the AAF doesn't carry are flagged. Premiere's Transform, Vector Motion and Warp Stabilizer write no values into an AAF. Those clips are flagged "not read": the reference is the place to see them.
  • A pull that was cut short is taken up again. Stop a pull, or lose one to a failed plate or a shut Mac, and the next pull finishes what wasn't done and leaves the finished plates alone. The button reads Pull N Remaining. From Terminal: --unfinished.
  • Each plate has its own versions and a record. Pulling a finished plate again writes v002 beside v001. A finished version has a small JSON record beside its folder: the source file, the frames, the handles, the color spaces, the retime and the reposition.
  • Network camera drives are said up front. When camera files are on a network volume, the Pull Plates window says how many plates will be copied to this Mac first. Over a remote link that is slow: pull from a locally mounted camera drive when you can.
  • One exception to "nothing is written over". Plates pulled with builds 1417 or 1421 have no record, so the next pull rewrites their newest version in place instead of writing the next one.
Earlier updates

1.0 (build 1421) Oct 11, 2026

  • ARRIRAW plates. Pull Plates now writes plates from ARRIRAW, HDE and ARRICORE camera files. ARRI Reference Tool develops each frame to linear ACES, so there is no curve or EI to choose, and Asobi converts it to ACEScg or ACES2065-1 and writes the EXR. The tool has to be on this Mac: the manual's Camera raw section has the steps.
  • Camera metadata in every plate. The camera's model, serial number, ISO, shutter, lens data and the rest of ARRI's header are carried into each EXR, with the source timecode and the true frame rate.
  • Camera files on a network volume are copied first. The frames a plate needs are trimmed to this Mac, then developed. The row says so while it happens. This is slow over a remote link: 14 frames took nearly three minutes through the tunnel to Kura. Pull from a locally mounted camera drive when you can.
  • Room on disk. The window says about how much the plates will take. A pull that doesn't fit is not started. Open-gate ARRIRAW is about 45 MB a frame as ZIP, so a 20-shot cut is about 40 GB.
  • Not yet. Folders of .ari frames, RED, Blackmagic RAW and DPX are listed and not pulled. ARRI's ProRes MXF goes the same way as ARRIRAW but has not been tried on a real file.

1.0 (build 1417) Oct 11, 2026

  • Pull Plates. Pull Plates in the Conform window writes a cut's plates as half-float EXRs in ACEScg or ACES2065-1, ZIP or PIZ. The window shows the plan first: every plate, the file it comes from, its frame numbers on disk and its frame count. Pull writes what the table says.
  • From the camera original. A camera clip is pulled from the original the Conform window found for it, never from its proxy. A render or a stock clip is pulled from the file the cut plays.
  • Handles and numbering. Handles are counted in the cut's frames, so a 200% shot gets twice as many source frames. The cut's first frame is 1001 with handles below it, or frames are numbered by source timecode.
  • Camera files are read as the color space you choose. It is never assumed. Until you choose, camera files are not pulled.
  • Nothing is written over. A second pull writes v002 beside v001. Each EXR's header carries the source timecode, frame rate, reel name, shot and retime, and Check Frames runs over every plate.
  • What it reads today. ProRes and other movies macOS decodes (ProRes in 16-bit float) and EXR sequences. ARRIRAW and ARRI MXF, RED, Blackmagic RAW and DPX are listed and not pulled yet.
  • From Terminal. Asobi pull --session <saved session> --out <shots folder> runs the same pull on a session saved from a conformed cut.

1.0 (build 1409) Oct 11, 2026

  • A saved session keeps its cut. Save a conformed session and open it later: the Conform window lists the cut again, with each shot's camera original as it was found, whether or not the camera drive is mounted. Look Again searches the camera folders afresh.
  • Offline shots stay in a reopened session. Opening a conformed session used to drop the shots whose media wasn't on disk, and failed to open when the first shot was offline. They stay, and the session opens on the first shot that has media. A new conform does the same.
  • Search Another Folder is in the Conform window. When media is missing, a Media row says how many clips aren't on disk and searches another folder for them. The alert that asked before the window opened is gone. Drop Missing Clips went with it: delete the clips in the playlist.
  • A freeze holds. A freeze frame in a cut flashed past in one frame. It now stays for as long as the cut holds it.

1.0 (build 1405) Oct 11, 2026

  • The Conform window. After a cut is conformed, a window lists every shot with its track, cut timecode, source range and speed, and what needs checking. Stacked layers sit under their plate. Graphics and slugs are listed too, found or not. Click a row to jump to that clip; the window follows the playhead. Window, Conform opens it again.
  • Camera originals. When a cut was made with proxies, choose the camera folders in the Conform window. Asobi finds each camera clip's original by name and checks the cut's timecode is inside that file. The Original column shows which were found, which to check and which are missing. The proxies still play; the originals are what a plate pull will read.
  • Proxy beside camera file. With A007C016.mov and A007C016.mxf on the same drive, the conform takes the file the cut names. A cut that gives only a clip name takes the one that plays.
  • Conform with nothing open. Media, Conform a Cut is available in an empty window.
  • As cut in Review Speed. A retimed clip's own speed is listed in Playback, Review Speed.

1.0 (build 1396) Oct 10, 2026

  • Conformed stacks are right. A letterbox matte or a legal card on an upper track used to pull every shot under it into one stack. A layer now joins only the shot it sits over. Graphics are set apart at the end as Graphics and References, and slugs with no media are left out.
  • Speed changes are read. A retime from Premiere (AAF), Resolve (OTIO) or an EDL is read the same way. The clip covers every source frame the event uses and plays at the cut's speed. Playback, Review Speed, Full speed shows it frame for frame. Speed ramps are not read yet.
  • Resolve OTIO cuts land on the right frame. Some clips started one frame early. Clips Resolve exports without a file path are kept and found by name.
  • The first conform in a new window loads. Conforming a cut with nothing else open gave an empty playlist.

1.0 (build 1389) Oct 10, 2026

  • Premiere EDLs conform. Import Cut for Conform refused every EDL saved with Windows line endings, which is how Premiere writes them, with "No events found". They read now.
  • Conformed clips start on the right frame. A cut names its sources by timecode. Asobi now finds that timecode inside each file. Before, a camera-timecode cut sent every clip to its file's last frame.
  • Per-track EDLs are one cut. Choose every EDL of a set (EDL 1, EDL 2, EDL 3) and the upper tracks stack with the shots they sit over.
  • OTIO cuts can be chosen in Import Cut for Conform, alongside AAF, XML and EDL. A cut's own frame rate is read from the cut, never assumed to be 24.

1.0 (build 1386) Oct 10, 2026

  • New Project… at the foot of Teams starts a project's team before its first review.
  • Rename a project from the Teams page (Rename…, or double-click its name) or by right-clicking it in the list. Remove Team… is there too.
  • Find a team. The project list filters by project or by person (type a name to see every team they're on) and sorts by Recently Used, Name or Most People.
  • Sort a team by clicking a column: Name, Email, Access, Opened. Longer teams get a filter.
